DAVIDAU DELETED MY POST AND BANNED ME FOR ASKING ABOUT BENCHMARKS — HERE IS THE FULL ANALYSIS (9B + 27B + 390 MODELS)

Community Article Published
August 11, 2026 Upvote 10 DedeProGames DedeProGames
I posted a discussion on the Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-711 model page asking for modern benchmarks (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, GPQA, LiveCodeBench). DavidAU did not respond. He did not close the discussion. He deleted it and then blocked me from interacting with any of his repositories ("you're not enabled to interact with this user").

So now I'm posting this here. If he deletes this too, the community will see the pattern.

WHAT HAPPENED

I posted a discussion on DavidAU/Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-711-Uncensored-Heretic-NM-DAU-NEO-MAX-MTP-GGUF asking for SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, GPQA Diamond, LiveCodeBench, AIME, and HMMT scores
DavidAU deleted the post — not closed, deleted
He then blocked me from all his repositories
I can no longer post discussions, comments, or interact on any of his 390+ model repos

This is the same person who:

Closed Discussion #10 on the 9B model after user KottCh reported the model failed at a basic coding task (Fermat's factorization) — closed the next day, no response
Ignored FreeGoldRush when they directly asked for SWE-bench Verified scores in Discussion #1 on the 27B model
Pinned positive discussions (Discussion #11: "Perfect Tool Calling") while deleting critical ones
Responded to criticism with "Trust me bro, it's the best" when asked for real benchmark results

The pattern is clear: close, ignore, delete, ban. When the model fails — close the discussion. When someone asks for modern benchmarks — ignore them. When someone posts a critical analysis — delete it and ban the user.

THE TWO MODELS ANALYZED

Model 1: Qwen3.5-9B-The-Defiant-Fable-Uncensored-Heretic-NEO-IMATRIX-MAX-MTP-GGUF

419,415 downloads/month
Claims: "ABSOLUTE FIRE: 640 ARC-C for both 8bit and 4bit"
Claims: "Extreme intelligence in a small package. Jaw dropping performance."
Claims: "Model exceeds 7 of 7 benchmarks for Qwen 3.5 9B, Qwen3.5 27B, Qwen3.6 35B-A3B"

Model 2: Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-711-Uncensored-Heretic-NM-DAU-NEO-MAX-MTP-GGUF

1.6 million+ downloads, 25,000+ on GGUF per month, 1,500+ likes
Claims: "The first fine tune to exceed 700 'arc-c' (The OpenAI, Claude and Gemini 'zone of intelligence')"
Claims: "The 700 'intelligence club' is reserved for OpenAI, Claude and Gemini closed source models"
Claims: "This is the one they fear"

Both models use the exact same 7 benchmarks. Both make extraordinary intelligence claims based on those 7 benchmarks. Neither model has been tested on a single modern benchmark.

BOOLQ is identical on both models (0.895 = 0.895 on 9B, 0.910 = 0.910 on 27B). Zero improvement.
The "711" in the 27B model name = ARC-C 0.711. The base Qwen 3.6 27B scores 0.647. So the entire "zone of intelligence" claim is built on a 6.4% improvement on a single saturated benchmark.
On the 40B expansion (Qwen3.6-40B-Grand-Intelligence-Six-711-717-raw), ARC-C dropped from 0.711 to 0.695. The 40B is worse on the one benchmark that supposedly defines "intelligence." And the card still claims it operates at "OpenAI, Claude and Gemini" levels.

THE RESEARCH THAT INVALIDATES THE ARC-C CLAIM

A 2024 paper from Snowflake AI Research (Borchmann, arXiv:2412.17758 — "In Case You Missed It: ARC 'Challenge' Is Not That Challenging") directly demonstrated that ARC-C's perceived difficulty is an artifact of the evaluation setup, not the actual complexity of the questions:

When Llama 3.1 70B was evaluated with all answer options visible (how humans take tests), ARC-C accuracy jumped from 64% to 93% — a 29-point swing just from changing the format
31% of ARC-C questions are "hardly answerable in separation" — they require comparing options to answer, but get evaluated without showing all choices
OpenBookQA went from 48% to 89% with correct evaluation — meaning it's essentially "solved," and any score differences are eval artifacts
The authors' conclusion: "The previously perceived difficulty was primarily an artifact of the evaluation method rather than the tasks' complexity"

So ARC-C was never an "intelligence barrier." It was a formatting issue. The "700 club" isn't some exclusive frontier model zone — it's a number that moves 29 points depending on how you set up your evaluation harness.
OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini do not compete on ARC-C. They don't report it. They don't market around it. They compete on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, GPQA Diamond, LiveCodeBench, AIME, and HMMT.

The irony: the Qwen 3.5 9B official model card is literally copy-pasted inside DavidAU's README — showing all 25+ modern benchmarks that Qwen reports. He includes the card showing what the base model can do on SWE-bench, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, BFCL, TAU2-Bench — and then tests his fine-tune on none of them.

THE CLOSED/DELETED/IGNORED DISCUSSIONS

"Thinking mode for precise coding tasks with temperature=0.6 also did not succeed"

I posted a discussion asking for modern benchmarks. DavidAU deleted it and blocked me from all his repositories.
The pattern: close, ignore, delete, ban.

THE GGUF QUALITY SITUATION

Custom quantization methods with no verification

DavidAU uses custom methods that don't exist in standard llama.cpp:

"NEO IMATRIX" — custom imatrix, no published calibration data, no perplexity measurements, no comparison to standard imatrix
"DI-MATRIX" — "averages of 2 imatrix datasets" — which datasets? What calibration text? How many chunks?
"TRI-MATRIX" — "averages of 3 imatrix datasets" — same questions
Output tensor modifications — "full precision - 16 bit" for all quants, no explanation of perplexity impact
MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) GGUFs — MTP tensors set to Q8_0, no documentation on quality impact

The model card claims NEO IMATRIX "improve accuracy of the quants by an additional 2-4% over normal GGUFs." 2-4% improvement is a significant claim with zero evidence.

Legacy quants

Research on llama.cpp quantization is clear:

Q4_0 has roughly 5x the perplexity error of Q4_K_M at nearly identical file size
Legacy quants (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1) use uniform scalar quantization — inferior to K-quants
IQ quants without a proper model-specific imatrix are usually worse than the equivalent K-quant
Double quantization "can severely reduce quality" — llama.cpp refuses this by default

DavidAU frequently uses legacy quants (Q5_1, Q4_1) instead of K-quants (Q5_K_M, Q4_K_M) with no explanation.

Flash attention issues

On GLM-4.7-Flash models, DavidAU's own card notes: "Quants prior to this commit (as well as Imatrix generation) performed poorly." and "Disable Flash Attn until this issue is resolved."

THE SCALE OF THE PROBLEM

DavidAU has 5 collections on Hugging Face:

Qwen 3.6 fine-tunes: 17 models

Total: approximately 390+ unique model repos. Combined downloads across these models are in the millions.
390+ models. Same 7 saturated benchmarks. Every. Single. Time.
And now, when someone asks for modern benchmarks, the response is to delete the post and ban the user.

THE PRESENTATION PROBLEM

Model names

Qwen3.5-9B-The-Defiant-Fable-Uncensored-Heretic-NEO-IMATRIX-MAX-MTP-GGUF — 80 characters. Compare with Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B — clean, identifiable.
Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-711-Uncensored-Heretic-NM-DAU-NEO-MAX-MTP-GGUF — 68 characters. Compare with Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B — clean, identifiable.

README content

The 9B README is 145 KB. Most model cards are 2-10 KB. This one includes:

Marketing claims ("ABSOLUTE FIRE," "Jaw dropping performance," "Extreme intelligence")
The entire Qwen 3.5 9B official model card copy-pasted (thousands of words)
4 full example generations (a ~2000-word cooling essay, a ~2000-word horror story with graphic gore, a ~1000-word self-promotional pitch with profanity, a ~2000-word Black Mirror episode set)
A random GIF (neo-dodge.gif, 4.22 MB)

The 27B README opens with:

"The strongest, smartest open source multi-stage model fine tune for consumer hardware ever and BUILT on consumer hardware via Unsloth."

And later: "This is the one they fear."
Compare with the Qwen 3.6 27B official model card: structured sections, 25+ benchmark tables, evaluation methodology footnotes (SWE-bench setup, Terminal-Bench harness, temperature, top_p, context window, number of runs), architecture specs, reproducible quickstart code, BibTeX citation. Night and day.

Reproducibility

Zero reproducibility in either model card. No eval scripts. No prompts. No harness config. No few-shot setup. No temperature. No sampling parameters. Just a bar chart from "Nightmedia" with no methodology. The Qwen 3.6 card tells you exactly how each benchmark was run. These cards tell you to trust a bar chart.

FINE-TUNING CAN IMPROVE LEGACY BENCHMARKS WHILE DEGRADING REAL CAPABILITIES

This is well-documented. Fine-tuning is not free. When you train a model to perform better on specific benchmarks, you can easily degrade its performance on other tasks — especially agentic ones.
The 9B model card even says "ZERO 'benchmaxing' (it damages the model)" — but then only reports the 7 saturated benchmarks where the fine-tune improved. We have zero information about whether this fine-tune:

Maintained the base model's 66.1 BFCL-V4 score (function calling)
Maintained the 79.1 TAU2-Bench score (agent benchmark)
Maintained the 65.6 LiveCodeBench v6 score (competitive coding)
Maintained the 81.7 GPQA Diamond score (PhD-level reasoning)
Maintained the 91.5 IFEval score (instruction following)
Can still do tool calling without loops (a user on the 27B model reported "looping tool calls")
Can still navigate OS environments (OSWorld: 41.8, AndroidWorld: 57.8)

The "human testing" claim — "the final testing was HUMAN testing. A trust, but verify approach" — is not a substitute for standardized benchmarks. "Human testing" with no methodology, no documented prompts, no reproducibility, and no published results is just anecdote.

WHAT I'M REQUESTING

1. Run the modern benchmarks. SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench v6, AIME26, HMMT Feb 26, SuperGPQA, BFCL-V4, TAU2-Bench. If the models truly operate in the "OpenAI, Claude and Gemini zone of intelligence," proving it on these benchmarks should be trivial.
2. Publish evaluation details. Which harness, what prompts, what few-shot config, what temperature, what sampling params, what context window, how many runs averaged. The Qwen team publishes all of this. SGLang, vLLM, KTransformers — all documented. These model cards have none of that.
3. Show perplexity numbers for the GGUFs. Compare each quant against F16 baseline using llama-perplexity. Compare NEO IMATRIX vs standard imatrix. Compare against quants from Bartowski or mradermacher. If the custom methods improve quality, the perplexity numbers will show it.
4. Explain the legacy quant choices. Why Q5_1 and Q4_1 instead of Q5_K_M and Q4_K_M? The K-quants are well-documented to be superior at similar file sizes.
5. Stop deleting and banning users who ask questions. I posted a discussion asking for modern benchmarks. The post was deleted and I was banned. Discussion #10 showing the model failing at coding was closed. FreeGoldRush's SWE-bench request was ignored. This is not how open-source communities work.

BOTTOM LINE

I'm not saying these models are bad. I genuinely don't know — and that's the problem. The only evidence provided is a set of 2018 benchmarks that research has shown to be unreliable discriminators, presented alongside marketing language ("This is the one they fear," "ABSOLUTE FIRE") and with zero modern benchmark coverage, zero reproducibility, and zero GGUF quality verification.
And when someone asks for modern benchmarks, the response is to delete the post and ban the user.
If the models are as good as claimed, proving it on SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, and GPQA should be easy. If they're not, then the community deserves to know that too — before another million people download a model based on 2018 science quiz scores.
Show us the SWE-bench score. Show us the Terminal-Bench score. Show us the GPQA Diamond score.
If the claims hold up, I'll be the first to celebrate. But I need numbers, not slogans. And I need the right to ask questions without being banned.

If this post gets deleted too, that will be the most honest response possible — not in words, but in action.
